headline: Dōryō is borrowed from Middle Chinese 同僚 (MC duwng lew).

sources.quote: Borrowed from Middle Chinese 同僚 (MC duwng lew).

headline: Sasayaku is ささ (sasa, an onomatopoeia) plus the verb-forming suffix やく (-yaku).

sources.quote: ささ (sasa, an onomatopoeia) + やく (-yaku, a verb-forming suffix attaching to mimetic words)

headline: Juwaki is 受話 (juwa, “listening on a telephone”) plus 器 (-ki, “device”).

sources.quote: 受話(じゅわ) (juwa, “listening on a telephone”) + 器(き) (-ki, “device”)

headline: Michijun is 道 (michi, “way”) plus 順 (jun, “order”).

sources.quote: From 道 (michi, “way”) + 順 (jun, “order”).

meaning: to appear (in print), to be recorded
headline: Noru, “to appear in print”, is cognate with 乗る (noru).

sources.quote: Cognate with Japanese 乗(の)る (noru).

headline: Hokori, “pride”, is the continuative stem of 誇る (hokoru, “to be proud of”).

sources.quote: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 誇(ほこ)る (hokoru, “to be proud of”).

meaning: to be piled up, lie on top of one another
headline: Kasanaru is from Old Japanese; compare 嵩む (kasamu, “to increase”).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. Compare 嵩(かさ)む (kasamu, “to increase”), かさ張(ば)る (kasabaru, “to grow bulky”).

headline: Shimatta is the perfective of しまう (shimau, “to finish”): literally “finished”.

sources.quote: The perfective form of しまう (shimau, “to finish”), literally meaning “finished”. Compare Mandarin 完了 (wánle).

headline: Kumu, “to serve sake”, is likely the same word as 汲む (kumu, “to pour”).

sources.quote: Likely the same word as 汲(く)む (kumu, “to pour”) and 斟(く)む (kumu, “to consider people's feelings”).

meaning: to be caught in, to be stuck in
headline: Hikkakaru is a sound shift from ひきかかる (hikikakaru).

sources.quote: Sound shift from ひきかかる (hikikakaru).

headline: Dan, “step”, is from Middle Chinese 段.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 段 (MC dwanH).

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Kōsa is Middle Chinese 交叉, with 差 a daiyōji replacing 叉.

sources.quote: Middle Chinese 交叉
差 is a daiyōji replacing 叉.

headline: Kaikan is from Chinese 會館 (huìguǎn), analyzable as 会 (kai, “meeting; gathering”) plus 館 (kan, “public building”).

sources.quote: From Chinese 會館 /会馆 (huìguǎn). Analyzable as 会 (kai, “meeting; gathering”) + 館 (kan, “public building”).

meaning: to sleep; to go to sleep; to go to bed
headline: Neru is from Old Japanese 寝 (nu).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese 寝 (nu).

headline: Zen, “good”, is from Middle Chinese 善.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 善 (MC dzyenX).

headline: Oshimai is 御 (o-, beautifying prefix) plus しまい (shimai, “ending, finishing”).

sources.quote: Compound of 御(お) (o-, beautifying prefix) + しまい (shimai, “ending, finishing”, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb しまう (shimau, “to finish, to end”)).

headline: Mukau is a shift from 向き合う (mukiau).

sources.quote: Shift from 向(む)き合(あ)う (mukiau).

headline: Kantai, the “frigid zone”, is 寒 (“cold”) plus 帯 (“belt”).

sources.quote: 寒 (“cold”) + 帯 (“belt”)

meaning: to pass (e.g., car), to outdistance, to outstrip
headline: Oikosu is 追う (ou, “to chase”) plus 越す (kosu, “to go past”).

sources.quote: 追(お)う (ou, “to chase”) + 越(こ)す (kosu, “to go past”)

headline: Aratamete is the -te form of the verb 改める (aratameru).

sources.quote: From the -te conjunctive form of verb 改める (aratameru).

headline: Nashi is the classical terminal form of the modern adjective 無い (nai).

sources.quote: Classical terminal form of the modern adjective 無(な)い (nai).

headline: Kappu is English cup, a doublet via Late Latin cuppa of コップ (koppu).

sources.quote: From English cup. Doublet (via Late Latin cuppa) of コップ (koppu), from Dutch kop and Portuguese copo.

headline: Osoroshii is an adjectivization of the verb 恐る (osoru, “to fear”).

sources.quote: Adjectivization of verb 恐(おそ)る (osoru, “to fear”).

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Masatsu is a Middle Chinese compound, 摩擦 (MC ma tshat).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 摩擦 (MC ma tshat).

headline: Bushu, “radical”, is from Middle Chinese 部首, first mentioned in Chinese in the Shūowén Jiězì of roughly 100 CE.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 部首 (MC buX syuwX). First mentioned in Chinese in the Shūowén Jiězì of roughly 100 CE.

headline: Arai is cognate with 粗い (arai).

sources.quote: Cognate with 粗(あら)い (arai).

meaning: to expand, to swell (out), to become inflated
headline: Fukuramu, “to swell”, is 膨 (fukura, “a bulge, a swelling”) plus -mu, first cited to the mid-800s.

sources.quote: First cited to the mid-800s.

From 膨, 脹 (fukura, “a bulge, a swelling”) + む (-mu, suffix indicating “looks like, seems like”). The fukura portion is in turn from now-archaic verb 膨る, 脹る (fukuru, “to swell, to bulge”), superseded by modern 膨れる, 脹れる (fukureru) of the same meaning.

headline: Massaki is 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) plus 先 (saki, “first”).

sources.quote: From 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) + 先 (saki, “first”).

headline: Ji, “character”, is from Middle Chinese 字.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 字 (MC dziH).

meaning: to avoid (physical contact); to ward off, to avert
headline: Sakeru is from 避く (saku), cognate with 裂ける (sakeru).

sources.quote: From 避(さ)く (saku), cognate with Japanese 裂ける (sakeru). See the page for 避(さ)く (saku) for more information.

headline: Kō, “this way”, shifted from 斯く (kaku): kaku, kau, kɔː, then kō.

sources.quote: /kaku/ → /kau/ → /kɔː/ → /koː/
Shift from 斯(か)く (kaku).
